chunks: Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa narrated: He said to me, Abu Ali ibn al-Junayd said to me, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shalmaghani said:

"We did not enter into this matter with Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) except while we knew what we were entering into. We were fighting each other for this position like dogs fight over a corpse." Abu Muhammad said: "The Shia did not pay attention to this saying and remained united in cursing him and disavowing him."

key_terms.أَبِي الْقَاسِمِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ رُوحٍ: Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, a prominent Shia secretary during the Minor Occultation
key_terms.الْبَرَاءَةِ: Disavowal or dissociation, indicating the Shia's unified stance regarding the matter
key_terms.الْجِيفِ: Corpse or carcass, used metaphorically for the coveted position

ai.seo_question: How did the Shia community view the intense competition among officials during the era of al-Husayn ibn Ruh?
ai.summary: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shalmaghani recounts that entering the service of the prominent secretary Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh involved intense competition, which he vividly illustrates by comparing the struggle to dogs fighting over a carcass. While the Shia community ultimately accepted this reality and remained united in their regard for him, the metaphor highlights the fierce rivalry and high stakes associated with securing a key position in the Four Deputies' administration during the Minor Occultation.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 361 - Abu Muhammad Harun Ibn Musa says: Abu Ali Junaid said to me, Abu Ja’far Muhammad Ibn Ali Shalmaghani said, “

I did enter into this contest against Abul Qasim Husain Ibn Rauh, but I knew what I was entering into. We were fighting each other for this position like dogs fight each other over a corpse.” Abu Muhammad said: “The Shia did not pay attention to these words and were unanimous in praying for his chastisement and despising him.”
